## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-*juǎn* Northern-Sòng translation of an Indian *Kāyatrayastotra*, in praise of the three bodies of the Buddha. Translated by [法賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%B3%A2) Fǎxián at the Sòng Institute. The author is identified only generically as 西土賢聖 ("the worthies and sages of the Western Land [= India]"), the standard Sòng convention for naming an Indian author whose specific identity had not been preserved.

**Abstract**

The *Fó sānshēn zàn* is a slightly longer *trikāya* hymn than the parallel [KR6o0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0132) *Sānshēn fàn zàn* (also translated by Fǎxián). Both texts attest the late-Indian *Kāyatrayastotra* tradition, of which the Tibetan canon preserves an independent witness. The Sòng translation is bracketed by Fǎxián's Institute career, 982–1000. The Taishō uses 高麗 as base.
